title: How to Extract Text from Images and Screenshots in Bulk
metaTitle: Extract Text from Images & Screenshots in Bulk (OCR)
metaDescription: Extract text from screenshots, photos and receipts in bulk with OCR. Pick the right segmentation mode, filter noisy words and redact with word boxes.
summary: Send image URLs to the Image to Text OCR actor, use the `sparse` segmentation mode for screenshots, and read the text and confidence per image. It costs $3 per 1,000 images.
intro: Copying text out of one screenshot is easy. Doing it for a few thousand support screenshots, receipt photos or saved social posts is not, and the results vary a lot depending on whether the image is a clean UI capture or a skewed phone photo.

Generic OCR settings are tuned for full pages of text, so they often miss the scattered labels in a screenshot or merge columns in a receipt. The Image to Text OCR actor runs Tesseract 5 with a choice of page segmentation modes, returns a confidence score per image, and can return every word with its pixel box.
This guide picks settings for different image types, filters out unreliable results in Python, and uses word boxes to find and redact sensitive text.

steps.name: Get public links to the images
steps.text: The actor reads images by URL: PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP and JPEG 2000. HEIC and AVIF photos from phones and SVG are not supported, so convert photos to JPEG first. Files can be up to 100 MB each.

steps.name: Pick a segmentation mode for the image type
steps.text: `pageSegmentation` controls how Tesseract looks for text. `auto` suits photos of documents and scanned pages. `sparse` looks for text anywhere and is the best start for UI screenshots, forms and infographics. `single-block` suits receipts and short snippets, and `single-column` suits uniform text. If you are unsure, run a small sample of images in two modes and compare confidence scores.

steps.name: Set languages and noise filtering
steps.text: Choose up to 4 of the 29 languages in `languages`; screenshots from a localised app may need two. `minWordConfidence` drops words Tesseract is unsure about, which helps with compression artefacts, icons mistaken for letters and background patterns. Start around 40-60 and lower it if real words go missing.

steps.name: Keep reliable results and queue the rest
steps.text: Each image is one row with `text`, `wordCount` and `confidence`. Very low confidence or very few words usually means a blurry photo, handwriting or an image with no real text. Split results into accepted and needs-review lists.

steps.name: Find and redact sensitive text with word boxes
steps.text: Turn on `includeWords` to get every recognised word with its confidence and pixel box (left, top, width, height). The exact field names inside each word entry can be checked in your first run's dataset; the snippet below reads them defensively. With Pillow you can then draw filled rectangles over matching words, for example email addresses, before sharing the screenshot.

code.code:
import io, re
import requests
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

EMAIL = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+")

def redact(row, out_path):
    img = Image.open(io.BytesIO(requests.get(row["url"], timeout=60).content)).convert("RGB")
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    for w in row.get("words") or []:
        text = w.get("text", "")
        if EMAIL.search(text):
            box = w.get("bbox") or w
            l, t = box["left"], box["top"]
            draw.rectangle([l, t, l + box["width"], t + box["height"]], fill="black")
    img.save(out_path)

steps.name: Mix in scanned PDFs if you need to
steps.text: Scanned PDFs work in this actor too, page by page. If your batches regularly mix PDFs and images, [OCR to Text](actor:ocr-to-text) uses the same engine and pricing and is set up for mixed document intake.

costExample: Extracting text from 2,500 support screenshots costs 2,500 x $0.003 = $7.50, with no compute charge on top. Images that fail to download or turn out blank are not charged.
tips: Low-resolution thumbnails OCR badly; link to the full-size image whenever you can.
Images rotated by 90 or 180 degrees are not auto-rotated; slightly skewed photos are fine.
Handwriting and decorative fonts come out poorly. Use the confidence score rather than assuming every result is usable.
Charts and pictures with no text return little or nothing; that is expected, not an error.

faq.q: What is the best OCR setting for screenshots?
faq.a: Start with `pageSegmentation` set to `sparse`, which looks for text anywhere on the image rather than assuming a page layout. Compare it with `auto` on a few samples and keep the one with higher confidence.

faq.q: Can I extract text from images on a web page?
faq.a: Yes, if you have the direct image URLs. Collect the image links first, then pass them in `urls`. Links that return a web page instead of an image are reported and not charged.

faq.q: Does OCR keep the layout of the screenshot?
faq.a: It keeps line and paragraph breaks in reading order, not the visual layout. For positions, turn on `includeWords` to get each word's pixel box.

faq.q: How do I process thousands of images?
faq.a: Pass them in batches via `urls`; `maxFiles` defaults to 1,000 per run and can go up to 10,000. Set a maximum total charge so a large batch stops cleanly at your budget.
